p: there were false prophets also among: As in times past there were two kinds of prophets, the one true and the other false, so Peter tells them that there will be true and false teachers in the Church, so much so that Christ himself will be denied by some, who nonetheless will call him redeemer.
people: Under the law, while the state and policy of the Jews was yet standing.
And many shall follow their pernicious: There shall not only be heresies, but also many followers of them.
And through covetousness shall they with: Covetousness for the most part is a companion of heresy, and makes trade in souls.
merchandise of you: They will abuse you, and sell you as they sell cattle in an auction.

whose judgment now of a long: Comfort for the godly: God who cast the angels that fell away from him, headlong into the darkness of hell, to eventually be judged; and who burned Sodom, and saved Lot, will deliver his elect from these errors, and will utterly destroy those unrighteous.
hell: So the Greeks called the deep dungeons under the earth, which should be appointed to torment the souls of the wicked in.
chains of darkness: Bound them with darkness as with chains: and by darkness he means that most miserable state of life that is full of horror.
old world: Which was before the flood: not that God made a new world, but because the world seemed new.
preacher of righteousness: For one hundred and twenty years, he did not cease to warn the wicked both by word and deed, of the wrath of God hanging over their heads.
seeing and hearing: Whatever way he looked, and turned his ears.
vexed his righteous soul from day: He had a troubled soul, and being vehemently grieved, lived a painful life.
knoweth how to deliver the godly: Has been long practised in saving and delivering the righteous.

But chiefly them that walk after: He goes to another type of corrupt men, who nonetheless are within the bosom of the Church, who are wickedly given, and do seditiously speak evil of the authority of magistrates (which the angels themselves that minister before God, do not discredit.) A true and accurate description of the Romish clergy (as they call it.)
dignities: Princes and great men, be they ever so high in authority.

But these: An accurate description of the same persons, in which they are compared to beasts who are made for destruction, while they give themselves to fill their bellies: For there is no greater ignorance than is in these men: although they most impudently find fault with those things of which they know not: and it shall come to pass that they shall destroy themselves as beasts with those pleasures with which they are delighted, and dishonour and defile the company of the godly.
made to be taken and destroyed: Made to this end to be a prey to others: So do these men willingly cast themselves into Satan's snares.
own corruption: Their own wicked conduct shall bring them to destruction.

while they feast with you: When by being among the Christians in the holy banquets which the Church keeps, they would seem by that to be true members of the Church, yet they are indeed but blots on the Church.

Having eyes full of adultery: He condemns those men, showing even in their behaviour and countenance an unmeasurable lust, making trade of the souls of vain persons, as men exercised in all the crafts of covetousness, to be short, as men that sell themselves for money to curse the sons of God in the same way Balaam did, whom the dumb beast reproved.

These are: Another note by which it may be known what manner of men they are, because they have inwardly nothing but that which is utterly vain or very harmful, although they make a show of some great goodness, yet they shall not escape unpunished for it, because under pretence of false freedom, they draw men into the most miserable slavery of sin.
wells without water: Who boast of knowledge and have nothing in them.
darkness is reserved for ever: Most gross darkness.
swelling words of vanity: They deceive with vain and swelling words.
allure through the lusts of the: They take them, as fish are taken with the hook.
clean escaped from them who live: Unfeignedly and indeed, clean departed from idolatry.
For if after they have escaped: It is better to have never known the way of righteousness, than to turn back from it to the old filthiness: and men that do so, are compared to dogs and swine.
